judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer mentions pysersic in the context of Section 3.1 discussing the fit quality, but never challenges the methodological characterization of pysersic or flags that the Bayesian qualifier is missing. No flag corresponds to the claim_methodology_drift injection.

The review mentions 'The pysersic fit for Jekyll/Hyde appears in Figure 3 only for F277W' but does not challenge the claim that pysersic is Bayesian or otherwise mischaracterized relative to Pasha2023. Under the broadened-claim rule, this does not specifically contest the post-edit citation claim.

The reviewer mentions 'pysersic' in the context of requesting fit residuals in Figure 3, but they do not challenge the description of the code or its characterization relative to the Pasha & Miller 2023 citation as required by the detection rules.

The reviewer mentions pysersic in the context of the deblending section (Section 3.1) but only notes that residuals across multiple bands or goodness-of-fit metrics should be shown to build confidence in the deblending — they do not challenge the characterization of pysersic as non-Bayesian or flag the missing 'Bayesian' qualifier. No mention of the methodological characterization of the code itself.
